transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Lately I keep forgetting everyday things—calls I promised to make, appointments I just wrote down, even simple errands—and it’s starting to cause problems with my husband’s care. I've always managed to get by, but now it feels like I just can't keep it all straight anymore and it's really starting to worry me.
Along with these memory struggles, have you also been feeling down, depressed, or noticed a loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I don't feel depressed and I haven't lost interest in my usual activities. I just feel incredibly overwhelmed, stressed, and anxious that I'm going to make a serious mistake with my husband's care.
Aside from the trouble with appointments, are you still able to handle your own daily tasks—like managing your medications, preparing meals, and personal care—completely on your own?

I can still handle basic personal care like getting dressed, but managing the daily household tasks has become quite difficult. I find myself getting distracted while cooking and losing my place in recipes, constantly misplacing my own pill organizer, and forgetting simple chores like moving the laundry to the dryer.
Even though these household tasks and managing your medication have become difficult, are you still able to complete them on your own without needing help from others?

Yes, I am still trying to handle all of these tasks on my own because I'm my husband's primary caregiver, but I feel like I'm barely keeping my head above water. I haven't asked anyone for help yet, but I've had to pull back from my volunteering and church activities just to try to keep up. I'm constantly terrified that I'm going to make a serious mistake, especially after I almost mixed up my husband's medication timing.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your memory and managing your daily tasks?

While I've had minor habits like this my whole life, these difficulties have really stood out and interfered with my daily life for about a year and a quarter. It became a real problem when my husband's health declined and I had to take on his caregiving and appointment scheduling.
Have you been diagnosed with any physical medical conditions, or have you experienced any recent illnesses, infections, or head injuries?
No, I haven't had any recent illnesses, infections, or head injuries. When my primary care doctor referred me here, she didn't mention any physical medical conditions that could be causing this.
Have you had any difficulty managing your finances, such as paying bills or keeping track of your budget, and are you still able to do this on your own?

Yes, managing the bills has become very difficult for me lately. When I sit down to handle them, I just end up with piles of papers and half-filled calendars all over the dining table, and I can't seem to decide what to tackle first. It makes everything feel jumbled and rushed at the last minute, though I am still trying to do it myself.
Have you noticed any difficulty finding your way around familiar places, or have you experienced times where you felt confused about the date, the year, or where you were?

No, I don't have any trouble finding my way around familiar places, and I've never felt confused about the date, year, or where I am. My issues are really just about keeping track of my daily tasks and paying attention, rather than being disoriented like that.
While you are trying to manage everything yourself, have there been actual instances where bills went unpaid, medications were missed, or someone had to step in to help you correct a mistake?

Yes, and it's so embarrassing to admit, but I had a scary near-miss where I almost mixed up the timing of my husband’s medications, and a friend at church recently had to gently point out mistakes I was making with our volunteer work. As for the bills, I haven't actually missed a payment yet, but they get so piled up and jumbled on the table that I'm always rushing at the very last second to pay them.
Have you had to completely hand over any of your daily responsibilities—like managing finances, driving, or organizing medications—to someone else because you could no longer do them safely?

No, I haven't handed over any of those responsibilities to anyone else yet, and I'm still the one trying to manage my husband's medications, appointments, and our household. However, after that scary near-miss with his medicine timing, I did decide to completely pull back from my volunteering at the church and senior center because I'm just so afraid of making a serious mistake.
Did your primary care doctor run any specific tests, such as blood work or a brain scan like an MRI or CT, and if so, what were the results?

I don't recall my primary care doctor doing any brain scans like an MRI or CT, or any specific blood tests for this. She mostly just referred me directly for this evaluation to figure out what was causing my memory and attention issues.
Do you have any chronic medical conditions that you take daily medication for, such as high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid issues, or high cholesterol?
No, I don't have any major chronic medical conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes. I also don't take any daily prescription medications myself.
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your ability to express yourself, find the right words when speaking, or understand what others are saying?

I haven't really noticed any trouble finding the right words or expressing myself, and I can understand others just fine. However, I do sometimes miss what people say simply because I get easily distracted or my mind starts to wander.
When you try to focus on or complete these daily mental tasks, do you experience a strong sense of mental exhaustion or fatigue very quickly?

Yes, absolutely. If I know I have to sit and really concentrate on something, like filling out my husband's online insurance forms, my brain feels tired before I even start. I dread how quickly I'll lose track of what I'm doing, so I find myself making excuses to put those tasks off.

You mentioned having some minor habits like this your whole life. When you were a child or teenager, did you struggle with paying attention in school, organizing your work, or constantly misplacing things?

Yes, these difficulties actually go all the way back to my childhood. Even in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was a bright girl but always daydreaming and losing track of instructions, and I'd constantly forget to turn in my homework unless my mother stood over me and checked my backpack.
Along with the daydreaming and focus issues, did you also struggle with feeling restless, constantly on the go, or acting impulsively when you were younger?

No, I don't recall struggling with restlessness, being constantly on the go, or acting impulsively when I was younger. My difficulties back then were almost entirely about daydreaming, losing track of instructions, and forgetting to turn in my homework, which my teachers often noted on my report cards.

opening_question.question: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong history of severe inattention, organization difficulties, and forgetfulness that dates back to early childhood (as evidenced by school report cards noting daydreaming, losing track of instructions, and forgetting homework). While she managed to cope during adulthood, the increased cognitive demands of caring for her ailing husband decompensated her coping strategies, leading to significant functional impairment in managing medications, household chores, and finances. She denies symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity, consistent with a predominantly inattentive presentation of Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ICD-10 F90). Other medical, neurological, or depressive etiologies have been ruled out.
